Template: followup-item

Node type: followup-item
File naming: docs/followups/<slug>.followup.html, with no date on it
Purpose: one intention, with somewhere to land and nothing to keep current
Design: the spec for this family
Styling: ./followup.template.css, plus the shared ../theme.css

Why this template exists

Work interrupts itself. You sit inside one thing and notice another, and opening a parallel session costs more than the notice is worth. The thought needs somewhere to go in one line, and it needs to come back at the moment somebody can act on it.

The knowledge graph absorbed this for three weeks and it went badly. Eleven of its 578 titles read as a deferral, and two have been dead since January: one defers parsing to a version that never arrived, and one defers an implementation nothing here descends from. Nothing said so, because nothing was watching.

Seven of those eleven name no condition at all. A line reading settle the asymmetry in a follow-up is a wish rather than a deferral, and a reader cannot tell whether its moment arrived. The four that do name one point at something a person can check: until a second caller wants them, once the count reaches zero, when a check needs it.

Shape

Three fields, and the middle one carries the whole design. An item names a title, the place it applies, and what would end it. 

<followup-item>
  <followup-title>…</followup-title>
  <followup-at><a href="…">…</a></followup-at>
  <followup-when>… optional …</followup-when>
</followup-item>

The place is what makes an item survive

followup-at is required because it does two jobs no list can do. It puts the item in front of a reader the moment they open the thing it concerns, so nobody has to read a backlog to find it. And it dates the item against the repository rather than against a calendar.

every-link-resolves already fails a build on an href pointing at something that no longer exists, across the whole corpus and out to source files. So an item about a deleted file or a retired claim breaks validation. Staleness gets loud instead of piling up quietly, which is the failure those January deferrals demonstrate.

The link sits inside followup-at rather than carrying a data-rel of its own. The same move keeps grounding out of the canon's own edge vocabulary, and it works here for the same reason: containment already says what the link is, so no relation label has to.

Deletion is the success state

This is the only family here where removing a document means the work went well. A knowledge node is a dated record and an axiom is a claim somebody relied on, so deleting either one throws something away. An item exists in order to stop existing.

The ordinary way one goes is that a person does the thing and drops the note. Two more forces remove one, and they cover the items nobody acts on: the condition fires, or the place stops existing. Both come from outside the document.

So there is no status field and nothing to update. done deletes the file, and the command carries the meaning a field would try to store. Git holds every item this family ever carried, so what the project decided not to do last month stays answerable with nothing recording it.

The plan family shows the alternative. Twelve documents hold 286 statuses and every one of them says completed, which is what a maintained progress field becomes once everybody stops.

What an item never carries

Priority, size, assignment and ordering. Each one is a field somebody keeps current, and this project has 286 statuses showing where that ends. An item also carries no steps, because the spec or the plan it turns into holds those, and an item that grew steps stopped being an item some time ago.

A worked example

A sample <followup-item>, checked by template.template.html's generic validator against the attributes on the <template> above. mycelium validate finds it by its data-conforms-to the same way it finds every instance, so this file fails if it stops conforming.

Give a condition somewhere to run this family once the notebook family exists to share its runner

Authoring commands

add, list and done. Each command's own /** … */ comment is its only documentation, so mycelium followup --help and this page can never drift apart.

No due yet. A condition that a script answers wants the same runner a notebook experiment wants, and that family does not exist, so list prints the conditions and a person reads them. The worked example above is the item recording that.

Conformance

Conformance is a data-conforms-to attribute on the element making the claim, the same as every other family here. 

<followup-item data-conforms-to="../templates/followup.template.html#followup-item">
  …
</followup-item>
